newsitem.title: CANADA: DeBeers' Canada deal faces legal challenge.
newsitem.headline: DeBeers' Canada deal faces legal challenge.

text.p: A legal challenge has been mounted against a deal between three Canadian exploration companies and South Africa's De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd, but the Canadian partners do not expect the case to scuttle an agreement on a promising Arctic diamond property.

John Dupuis, president of Canamera Geological Ltd, has filed a lawsuit in the British Columbia Court of Appeal seeking an injunction against the agreement. The three firms -- Mountain Province Mining Inc, Glenmore Highlands Inc and Camphor Ventures Inc -- announced last month a deal with the De Beers' exploration unit Monopros Ltd.

Under the joint venture deal, Monopros can earn a 60 percent interest in the AK/CJ diamond property in Canada's Northwest Territories if it completes exploration work, sampling and a feasibility study and finances a mine.
Dupuis, who sold the property to Mountain Province, claims he had the right of first refusal if Mountain Province decided to sell, Mountain Province President Jan Vandersande told Reuters.
The court has granted an interim stay until the case is heard, he said.
Contacted by Reuters, Dupuis had no immediate comment.

Vandersande said lawyers have told the three companies that Dupuis' claim is without merit and the lawsuit is having no practical effect on the deal. "We believe he has no case and work is continuing," he said.
Because Monopros must meet many conditions before it gains control of the property, the vesting of its interest is probably two years away, he said.

That means the lawsuit is not having any practical effect on the deal for now, although theoretically the interim stay would bar the transfer to Monopros if Mountain Province sought to enact it right now.

Mountain Province holds half of the property, Glenmore 40 percent and Camphor 10 percent. At the time the option agreement was announced, the companies said they intended to consolidate their holdings in the diamond prospect under Mountain Province through a share exchange.
So far the exploration companies have discovered one kimberlite pipe on the property that contains an estimated 19 million tonnes of ore grading two carats a tonne.
A spokeswoman for Monopros in Toronto said the company was unable to comment on the lawsuit, which was being reviewed by its lawyers.
